items.text: On Linux, the "all in one window" setting is read once at launch, as on the Mac.
Linux release packages install and run from anywhere, and a .deb is built from the same tree.
Pasting a file copied in Explorer pastes its path, as the Mac does.
Linux panes keep their background tint across a relaunch and an agent recovery.
The stack-slide test now checks that a strip which stays folded slides with the run.
On Linux a closed tab comes back with Ctrl+Shift+Z.
A screen reader finds each tucked pane's strip as a button that brings the pane forward.
The commit guard keeps a staged exec bit instead of silently dropping it.
On Linux, an in-app ghoztty:// link to a window that is gone shows the Can't focus dialog.
The cleanup-screen test's "a kept item makes the box clean" check now says what it still counted when it fails.
A viewer pane keeps its scroll when its file is saved, even right after it opens or when the save lands in pieces.
A restored Linux launch runs its own -e command.
The Windows installer no longer carries ghoztty.com: it writes it from ghoztty.exe while installing.
